title: Space Tech Briefing — September 25, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts and welcome to your essential daily dose of cosmic news! It's Friday, September 25, 2026, and we are absolutely buzzing with the latest from beyond our blue marble. Let's dive right in!

First up, a huge win for international scientific collaboration and French expertise! NASA has officially selected PRIMAger, a cutting-edge far-infrared camera, to be one of the two primary instruments aboard the upcoming PRIMA mission. This is a testament to the incredible French know-how, spearheaded by experts at the CNES. PRIMAger's selection highlights a critical step forward in our ability to observe the universe in the far-infrared spectrum, promising groundbreaking new insights into cosmic phenomena. We're talking about peering into the cold, dusty corners of space where stars and planets are born. What an exciting development for global science!

Now, as we prepare for today's new discoveries, let's take a moment to look back at a major recent development that truly rocked the lunar landscape. Scientists, utilizing stunning imagery from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, have unveiled the largest impact crater discovered on the Moon in over a century! This colossal scar measures a staggering 222 meters in diameter and is surrounded by a distinctive seven-kilometer-wide "cold spot." Officially named in honor of the late American scientist Tom McGetchin, a renowned geologist and planetologist, this massive crater was formed between April 11 and May 22, 2024. Imagine this: an asteroid or comet, roughly the size of a three to six-story building, slammed into the lunar surface, creating a crater approximately 43 meters deep. It’s a powerful reminder of the dynamic forces constantly shaping our celestial neighborhood.

And that's your morning briefing from the world of space technology! What an incredible time to be looking up. Thank you for joining us, and make sure to tune in again soon for more cosmic updates. Have a stellar day!
